subject: SIG follow-up: ownership & evidence across Hosted / Dedicated / Private
messages:
From: Acme Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: clarification on deployment mode responsibilities

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the initial SIG package. The risk team has two sets of follow-ups that are blocking our internal approval: one focused on data custody (encryption keys, log retention, audit access) and another on network/isolation controls across your three deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private/VPC).

Could you provide concise, SIG-friendly language that distinguishes who owns keys, who can access audit logs, and which evidence artifacts map to each statement for each deployment? Examples or a short ownership matrix would be great. We also need to know if any controls differ when a customer elects to use a customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed keys.

Requested timeline: ideally by EOD Wed (21 Jul) to keep our procurement sprint on schedule.

Thanks,
Security Team - Acme
security@acme-corp.com

Attachments: none

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>, Jaya Patel <j.patel@acme-corp.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: clarification on deployment mode responsibilities

Hi team — thanks for the clear ask. We've pulled together a short ownership matrix and supporting diagrams that map each SIG statement to evidence artifacts. High-level summary below; the matrix is attached (sig_deployment_ownership_matrix_v3.xlsx) and includes links to the diagrams and draft SIG answer copy.

High-level distinctions (plain language):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Redwood operates the control plane and stores data in our multi-tenant environment. By default, Redwood manages encryption keys (Redwood-managed KMS). Customers may request Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) for certain enterprise contracts; in that case, we integrate with customer KMS providers where supported — note that BYOK availability depends on plan and region.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Dedicated pools run in isolated tenancy for the customer. Network isolation and compute are dedicated; Redwood operates the control plane unless the customer selects a Private control plane. Customers can choose customer-managed keys for Dedicated in most engagements; when they do, key access and key rotation responsibilities are transferred to the customer per the KMS agreement in the matrix.

- Private / VPC / On-prem: Customer provides the networking boundary (VPC or air-gapped environment) and retains primary control over keys and audit logs. Redwood provides an optional Private control plane for operational convenience; where customers manage keys and storage on-prem, Redwood never has direct access to plaintext data or key material.

Evidence we are attaching: network diagram for Hosted (hosted_network_diagram.pdf), deployment checklist for VPC (vpc_deployment_checklist.xlsx), and a short KMS options summary (kms_options_summary.docx). The matrix maps these artifacts to specific SIG questions and also calls out where we can provide SOC 2 test procedures.

I copied Lauren (legal) to keep alignment on the wording. If acceptable, we'll produce the final SIG answer wording and return it to you by tomorrow EOD.

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether Acme requires BYOK for your environment (simple yes/no).
- If yes, tell us target KMS provider (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / Google KMS) and whether you require HSM-backed keys.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Compliance & Security Programs
Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Attachments: sig_deployment_ownership_matrix_v3.xlsx, hosted_network_diagram.pdf, kms_options_summary.docx

Sofia / Lauren — drafting notes for the SIG answers below (these are suggested short-form statements that we can paste into the SIG response). I added callouts for evidence files to reference in the matrix.

1) Hosted (Redwood-managed environment) — suggested SIG text:
"Redwood operates the hosted inference environment. Customer content is encrypted at rest and in transit. By default, encryption keys are managed by Redwood's KMS; Redwood personnel do not have access to customer plaintext except as required for support under strict RBAC and audit controls. Evidence: hosted_network_diagram.pdf; SOC2 report section 4.2; audit-log-sample-2027Q2 (available on request)."

Evidence callout: attach hosted_network_diagram.pdf (network flows), SOC2 (redacted), audit-log-sample stub.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — suggested SIG text:
"Dedicated pools run in isolated tenancy for a single customer. Customers may elect to use customer-managed keys (BYOK). When BYOK is selected, cryptographic key control remains with the customer; Redwood integrates with customer KMS for encryption-at-rest. Evidence: sig_deployment_ownership_matrix_v3.xlsx; dedicated-deployment-handoff-checklist (internal)."

Callout: for Dedicated, we should explicitly note any exceptions for telemetry/metrics collection (we collect anonymized telemetry for operations; raw request payloads are not retained unless explicitly enabled).

3) Private (VPC / On-prem) — suggested SIG text:
"Private deployments place the inference runtime within customer-controlled networking and storage boundaries. Customers retain control of keys and audit logs; Redwood's access is governed by the customer's network and administrative controls or by a private control plane contract if selected. Evidence: vpc_deployment_checklist.xlsx; kms_options_summary.docx."

Also: suggested change to hosted statement to clarify that Redwood supports enterprise BYOK only after a legal/security engagement — to avoid implying immediate self-service BYOK for hosted plans.

Let me know and I'll format these into final SIG answer copy.

- Priyom (Applied ML / Infra)

Hi Jaya / Acme team —

Attached is our finalized response pack for the SIG follow-ups. Key points summarized below (copyable for your questionnaire):

- Hosted: Redwood manages keys by default (Redwood-managed KMS). Enterprise BYOK is supported via an engagement; Redwood will integrate with customer KMS providers where contractually agreed. Evidence: hosted_network_diagram.pdf; sig_deployment_ownership_matrix_v3.xlsx; SOC2 (redacted) — available on NDA.

- Dedicated: Isolated tenancy for one customer. BYOK is available in most Dedicated engagements; when enabled, the customer controls key material. Evidence: sig_deployment_ownership_matrix_v3.xlsx; dedicated-handback-checklist (internal). Also note: operational telemetry is collected for service health but raw request retention is configurable.

- Private / VPC / On-prem: Customer-controlled environment. Customer is responsible for KMS and audit log retention when resources are customer-hosted. Redwood access is only with customer network authorizations or per private control plane contract. Evidence: vpc_deployment_checklist.xlsx; kms_options_summary.docx.

I have included simple, SIG-friendly sentences in the attached matrix and a short appendix mapping each sentence to evidence. If this matches your need we can paste the exact phrasing into the SIG portal or provide a docx export.

Please confirm whether Acme wants me to: (A) paste these answers into the SIG portal on your behalf, or (B) send the docx for you to upload. Also send your BYOK preference if applicable.

Thanks — aiming to close this for your procurement sprint.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
